page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n4 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, mapped from 4 physical Intel cores with 2 threads per core. The memory configuration provides 32.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. This server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the n4-standard-8 in the average tier for most compute tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 1676.09 and 6902.54 respectively, both falling into the middle 50% performance bracket. Similarly, Geekbench scores of 1770.0 (single-core) and 6838.0 (multi-core) align with average expectations. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in specialized workloads. However, memory performance shows some limitations, with a PassMark memory score of 1809.35, categorized in the bottom 25%.

The server exhibits a notable performance drop during complex multi-threaded tasks and larger model processing. While single-threaded gzip compression (27.37 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (11.52 GB/sec) perform at average levels, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25% with a score of 36.22 GB/sec. For language model tasks, the server handles prompt processing for a 7B model at 49.59 tokens/sec, but text generation drops to a poor 6.31 tokens/sec. From a resource-density perspective, the n4-standard-8 offers a balanced profile for standard workloads, though the lack of local storage and lower memory performance relative to its dedicated CPU allocation represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications. This configuration is best suited for standard web serving, database operations, and general-purpose applications.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM on an x86_64 Intel architecture. Powered by 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, it includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX. The server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. Performance benchmarks generally place this instance in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6838.0 and a static web serving throughput of 12.95 GB/sec. However, memory performance is a relative bottleneck, as indicated by a PassMark memory score in the bottom 25%. Multi-threaded decompression and medium-sized LLM text generation also show weaker performance. This configuration is best suited for standard web serving, database operations, and general-purpose applications that do not require high-density memory throughput or intensive multi-threaded processing.
